children: New "Co-Sports Club" for Junior High School Students with Disabilities, Offering
— Featuring Para-Sports, No Disability Certificate Required, and a Comprehensive Support System

TOKYO, Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LEIFRAS Co., Ltd. (Nasdaq: LFS) (the "Company" or "Leifras"), a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement and a leading operator of children's sports schools and school club activity support businesses in Japan, today announced that it has been awarded the "Nagoya Weekend Club Activities: Activities for Persons with Disabilities" service contract (the "Contract") by the City of Nagoya (Nagoya City Board of Education). Under the Contract, the Company will launch the Co-Sports Club, a new club for junior high school students with disabilities (the "Club"). The Club is designed to address the social issue of securing accessible sports environments for students with disabilities, which represents an important issue alongside Japan's policy of transitioning school club activities to communities, and to build educational infrastructure that promotes inclusive access to sports opportunities.
Contract Overview
Club Name: Co-Sports Club
Contracting Authority: City of Nagoya (Nagoya City Board of Education)
Program Period: October 2026 to March 2027 (approximately 1–2 sessions per month; 10 sessions in total)
Eligible Participants: Students in special support classes at Nagoya municipal junior high schools, students in the junior high school divisions of special needs schools, etc.
Participation Fee: Free
Application Method: Applications accepted through the Nagoya Weekend Club Activities portal site
A Blind Spot in the Regional Transition of School Club Activities: "Lack of Opportunities for Students with Disabilities" and Background to the Contract

As the transition of school club activities to community-based organizations progresses across Japan, Nagoya City has begun its own transition through the "Nagoya Weekend Club Activities" initiative. However, during this transition process, the absence of community organizations that provide para-sports activities that are accessible to students with disabilities has become a serious social issue. Leifras was selected for the Contract based on its top-ranked position in school club activity support in Japan (according to Tokyo Shoko Research, as of December 2025) and its unique expertise in providing sports-based developmental support to children with varying developmental needs through its "LEIF after-school daycare" service, which supports children with disabilities or developmental characteristics through soccer therapy.
Initiatives and Value Provided by the Club
Under the concept of "Move Together, Grow Together," the Club will provide the following distinctive activities so that students with disabilities can participate with confidence.
No disability certificate required, participation free of charge, and a flexible environment allowing one-time participation and participation accompanied by a parent or guardian:

No disability certificate or similar documentation is required. Any student who requires accommodations during activities may participate free of charge. Each session is designed to last approximately 90 minutes. Students may attend every session or join individual sessions at their convenience. Parents and guardians are also welcome to participate alongside students, enabling flexible attendance suited to each family's needs.
A diverse range of programs and instruction that respects "each student's own pace":

Students can explore a wide range of activities, from traditional sports, such as soccer, baseball, basketball, track and field, and dance, to para-sports designed for participants of varying abilities, including boccia and Mölkky. The Club enables each student to experience physical activity at their own pace, without comparison to others.
A "comprehensive support system" with five instructors for a capacity of 15 students:

To ensure safety tailored to the needs of each participant, five instructors will be assigned for a maximum of 15 students. The Company will coordinate with parents and guardians in advance, provide individualized accommodations as needed, and create an environment in which every student can participate with confidence.
Why Leifras is Chosen: Five Advantages
Industry-leading Contract Track Record:

The Company holds the leading industry position with 381 contracted schools and 2,120 supported clubs, ranking first in Japan by the number of children's sports schools and the number of supported school club activities as of December 31, 2025, according to Tokyo Shoko Research.
Robust National Government Network:

As a member of the Nippon Sport Policy Commission and an official partner of the Japan Sports Association, Leifras collaborates closely with key organizations representing Japan's sports industry and private education sector to co-promote national policies.
Extensive Local Government Network:
The Company has partnered directly with 33 prefectures and 13 Tokyo special wards, accumulating substantial operational know-how tailored to region-specific educational needs.
Japan's Only Large-Scale Coaching Platform:

Currently operating across 47 prefectures, Leifras employs 1,055 full-time staff and 3,544 part-time employees. The Company has also established stable, exclusive recruitment pipelines through comprehensive alliances with educational institutions.
Safety-First Operational System:

Full-time employees of the Company manage and oversee club activity instructors, to ensure thorough adherence to proprietary training programs and regular field audits. Since launching the school club support business in 2013, the Company has maintained a record of zero major accidents or severe injuries.
Future Outlook: Toward Sustainable "Inclusive School Club Infrastructure"

Through this initiative, the Company aims to contribute to building an inclusive model for the community-based transition of school club activities in Nagoya City. Going forward, the Company expects to continue to support the development of sustainable "new sports infrastructure" in which all children, regardless of ability, can genuinely enjoy sports and grow.
About LEIFRAS Co., Ltd.

Headquartered in Tokyo, Leifras is a sports and social business company dedicated to youth sports and community engagement. The Company primarily provides services related to the organization and operations of sports schools and sports events for children. As of December 31, 2025, Leifras was recognized as one of Japan's largest operators of children's sports schools in terms of both membership and facilities by Tokyo Shoko Research. The Company's approach to sports education emphasizes the development of non-cognitive skills, following the teaching principle "acknowledge, praise, encourage, and motivate." The holistic approach that integrates physical and mental development sets Leifras apart in the industry. Building upon deep experience and know-how in sports education, Leifras also operates a robust social business sector, dispatching sports coaches to meet various community needs with the aim to promote physical health, social inclusion, and community well-being across different demographics.
For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://ir.leifras.co.jp/.
